title: How the Donner Party Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a discussion of the hoax "hufu" (a tofu meant to taste like human flesh) and a flawed HowStuffWorks article on the Donner Party. They then cover the Donner Party's 1846 overland journey: George Donner and James Reed, Lansford Hastings and the Hastings Cut-Off, the disastrous desert crossing, the snowbound camps at Truckee Lake and Alder Creek in the Sierra Nevada, the Forlorn Hope snowshoe group and its cannibalism, the Lewis Keseberg accusations, the relief parties, and the survivors and deaths. The episode ends with listener mail, a joke letter about the hosts being stuck in time.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

entities.name: The Immigrant's Guide to Oregon and California

segments.title: Opening banter and the hufu hoax
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about watching PBS American Experience, then discuss hufu, a tofu marketed as tasting like human flesh that turned out to be a hoax. They also mention that a HowStuffWorks article on the Donner Party contained errors.

segments.title: Donner and Reed and the California movement
segments.summary: The hosts introduce George Donner, a wealthy farmer, and James Reed, who financed the trip and had an elaborate double-decker wagon. Donner was elected captain. They explain the chuck wagon's origin with Charles Goodnight, then describe the push to settle California before the gold rush and Lansford Hastings's role in it, including John Sutter and Fort Sutter.

segments.title: The Hastings Cut-Off and the desert crossing
segments.summary: Hastings's book promoted a shortcut, the Hastings Cut-Off, that he had never driven with wagons. The party took it, and it added about three weeks instead of saving time. They lost wagons and oxen crossing the salt desert. Reed killed a man named Snyder in a fight and was banished. Charles Stanton had gone for provisions. Hastings left a note urging them to turn back, and the party continued on the southern route.
topics: Immigrants Guide to Oregon and California

segments.title: Snowbound camps in the Sierra Nevada
segments.summary: Back on the California Trail, the party reached the Sierra Nevada in November, faced an early snowstorm, and decided to wait out the winter. They made two camps, one at Truckee Lake and one at Alder Creek. The hosts read a diary entry describing the deep snow and abandoned wagons. Snowpack reached roughly thirty feet.

segments.title: Starvation and the Forlorn Hope
segments.summary: Food ran out in the camps. The hosts describe the people eating their animals, dog, hides, shoelaces, boiled blankets, and bones. Fifteen of the strongest, including two Indian guides, formed the Forlorn Hope snowshoe group to cross the mountains. Charles Stanton died after being left behind, and the group began discussing cannibalism in December.

segments.title: Cannibalism in the Forlorn Hope and the guides
segments.summary: The first Forlorn Hope member, Antoine, died and was eaten, followed by Jay Fosdick and others, with a rule that relatives would not eat relatives. The group turned on the two Indian guides, who fled and were later killed and eaten. The Forlorn Hope reached Fort Sutter after about thirty-three days, and Reed tried to organize a rescue but was affected by the Mexican-American War.
topics: Donner Party guides Lewis and Salvador

segments.title: Rescue parties, Keseberg, and survivors
segments.summary: Four rescue parties were sent from California. The first brought out seventeen survivors, and Reed led the second. Lewis Keseberg was found alone at the camp and accused of murder and cannibalism. He later sued for defamation and was awarded one dollar. The hosts discuss the lack of forensic evidence for cannibalism, and note that the Reed and Breen families had no deaths while all the Donners died. They close with the party's effect on immigration and the gold rush.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener letter in the voice of Doc Brown and Max Prince jokes about the hosts being stuck in time. Josh and Chuck mention social media and the video podcast Stuff from the Future, then sign off.
